description:
Wire the fail-closed signal through to the published contract, so a fallback-priced run reports cost_status "unavailable" rather than "normalized".

Status wiring: _normalized_cost_warnings (calculator.py:255-286) currently only inspects deployment metadata. Add a check that scans benchmark_cost.phase_costs[*].query_costs[*].pricing_details for the price_unavailable marker and emits a warning. The existing machinery then flips cost_status and NormalizedCost.__post_init__ guarantees no number ships with it. No new output contract is needed - "unavailable" is already contract-tested at tests/unit/scripts/explorer_pipeline/test_normalized_cost_contract.py:44.

Staleness (R9): is_pricing_stale currently appends a string to BenchmarkCost.warnings that never reaches the status evaluator, so a 313-day-old table still publishes "normalized". Route it into the same path. Safe to enable here because the data correction has already landed and reset the clock.

Interim region guard: Athena and Synapse serverless take no region argument and their docstrings falsely claim a flat $5.00/TB rate; Sao Paulo is $9.00/TB for both, a 44% understatement. The proper fix (region parameters) is deferred, so add a calculator-level guard: the calculator already has the region in platform_config, so it can mark the cost unavailable when the region falls outside the verified set (us/eu/ap) without changing any pricing.py signature. Both reviewers flagged that deferring this while claiming fail-closed would leave the promise publicly violated on the hottest path.

Expect a visible product change: runs that flip to unavailable drop out of explorer cost charts, the leaderboard, and the cost_safe eligibility class (displayEligibility.ts:102, chartRegistry.ts:114, compareSummary.ts:325-356, CostScatter.tsx:55-68). That is correct - a wrong number should not be charted - but it is visible, not silent. Consider whether EXPLORER_READ_MODEL_VERSION (_project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/contract.py:5) needs a bump to 11; its own changelog shows v7 was bumped for a semantics-only change because cached snapshots could be read under stale semantics.
